extraction.name: Common Corpus
extraction.description: An open dataset for language model pre-training composed of uncopyrighted or permissively licensed data. It contains about two trillion tokens, covers a wide variety of languages including low-resource ones, and includes a large portion of code data.
extraction.creator: Pierre-Carl Langlais; Carlos Rosas Hinostroza; Mattia Nee; Catherine Amett; Pavel Chizhov; Eliot Krzystof Jones; Irène Girard; David Mach; Anastasia Stasenko; Ivan P. Yamshchikov
extraction.inLanguage: en, fr, de, zh, it, es, ja, pl, la, nl, ru, ar, ko
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Common Corpus was assembled by aggregating and curating existing open datasets and collection-as-data initiatives from libraries, public institutions, and open portals, including data retrieved via raw text files, dumps, and API access, then dispatching them into subsets and post-processing/filtering them.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw/source data consisted of digitized newspapers, books, monographs, legal and administrative documents, and related texts from sources such as the Library of Congress, Europeana, Gallica, Biblioteca, USPTO, UN Digital Library, EU websites, and OECD; some were provided as raw text files, dumps, or via API/JSON API access.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The Common Corpus effort has been ongoing since 2024; included source materials span multiple periods, e.g. USPTO documents from 2019 to 2022, US PD Newspapers published between 1690 and 1963, Europeana Newspapers between 1618 and 1990, and German PD Newspapers between 1794 and 1957.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A multilingual toxicity classifier (Celadon) was trained from scratch on annotated samples to identify harmful content across five dimensions: race/origin bias, gender/sexuality bias, religious bias, ability bias, and violence/abuse.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Celadon (DeBERTa-v3-small toxicity classifier) was used to identify harmful content; Microsoft Presidio was used to identify and replace PII; OCRoscope and OCRerrcr were used to assess OCR quality; OCRonos was used for OCR correction; Segmentext was used for text segmentation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset has uneven language coverage, with shallow coverage for low-resource languages and stronger representation of European languages and historical/public-domain sources.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Common Corpus does not cover all available open data, has shallow low-resource language coverage, is sized mainly for pre-training limited-size models rather than larger ones, does not include instruction-tuning or specialized-task data, is not directly suitable for task-specific fine-tuning, and curation is imperfect with possible OCR errors and less-than-perfect toxicity/PII filtering accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is presented as supporting open science and legally compliant LLM development, reducing reliance on copyrighted or restricted web data and helping research and development adhere to regulatory norms.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Potential personally identifiable information (PII) may be present and was targeted for removal during curation, but removal is not guaranteed to be perfectly accurate.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Primarily intended for language model pre-training; suitable for pre-training limited-size models and can support creation of ethical fine-tuning datasets, but it is not directly suitable for instruction-tuning or task-specific fine-tuning.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is under ongoing expansion since 2024, with active collection of more European-language data through the LLMs4EU project and planned enlargement into African languages.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Open Culture data were post-processed, filtered, and dispatched into smaller individual subsets; some datasets were curated to include only specific language collections.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Dataset filtering and curation were applied; data were post-processed and filtered, and some datasets were curated using APIs.

name.evidence: In this paper, we introduce Common Corpus, the largest open dataset for language model pre-training.

description.evidence: The data assembled in Common Corpus are either uncopyrighted or under permissible licenses and amount to about two trillion tokens. The dataset contains a wide variety of languages, ranging from the main European languages to low-resource ones rarely present in pre-training datasets; in addition, it includes a large portion of code data.

creator.evidence: Pierre-Carl Langlais Carlos Rosas Hinostroza Mattia Nee Catherine Amett Pavel Chizhov Eliot Krzystof Jones Irène Girard David Mach Anastasia Stasenko Ivan P. Yamshchikov

isLiveDataset.evidence: we present Common Corpus, which has been an ongoing effort since 2024

rai:dataCollection.evidence: “Large portion of data in Open Culture part of the Common Corpus was built on top of the following collection-as-data initiatives” and “Combined with the other retrieved data, the collections were dispatched into smaller individual subsets... The Open Culture data in Common Corpus have been post-processed and filtered”

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: “Large portion of data in Open Culture part of the Common Corpus was built on top of the following collection-as-data initiatives”

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: “Chronicle America: about 100B words (150B tokens) of digitized US newspapers by the Library of Congress, made available as a raw text file.”; “Gallica: about 85B words of digitized French newspapers and monographs made available on the open data portal... through entire dumps or API access”; “The dataset was curated by using the Library of Congress JSON API.”

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: “Common Corpus, which has been an ongoing effort since 2024” ; “This dataset consists of actions from this agency from 2019 to 2022.” ; “The articles were published between the years 1690 and 1963.” ; “its articles were published between 1618 and 1990” ; “The articles were originally published between 1794 and 1957.”

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: “We created a multilingual toxicity classifier, Celadon13, a DeBERTa-v3-small model (∼140M parameters), which we trained from scratch on 2M annotated samples. Celadon identifies toxic and harmful content along five dimensions: race and origin-based bias, gender and sexuality-based bias, religious bias, ability bias, and violence and abuse.”

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: “We created a multilingual toxicity classifier, Celadon13, a DeBERTa-v3-small model”; “To identify and replace PII, we use Microsoft’s Presidio12”; “We developed two pipelines to determine the digitization quality... OCRoscope... OCRerrcr”; “We developed OCRonos11 model based on Llama 3 8B”; “For text segmentation, we developed Segmentext7”

rai:dataBiases.evidence: “even though the language diversity of the data is large, the coverage for low-resource languages is still shallow. We are developing in this direction, planning for enlargement of the corpora in African languages”

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: “Common Corpus is far from collecting the whole range of available open data”; “the coverage for low-resource languages is still shallow”; “Larger models, however will require significantly larger amounts of data”; “Common Corpus naturally does not contain data for instruction-tuning and any forms of specialized tasks. Therefore, it is not directly suitable for task-specific fine-tuning”; “none of the curation methods could naturally facilitate a hundred-percent accuracy. However, some issues, like OCR errors, present considerable challenges”

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: “we show that open LLM research and development is possible while meeting legal and regulatory requirements” and “we hope that Common Corpus will grow as a critical infrastructure for open science LLM research and development”

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: “we used these methods responsibly and mitigated many issues overlooked by the counterparts (e.g., with toxicity detection and PII removal), none of the curation methods could naturally facilitate a hundred-percent accuracy”

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: “we introduce Common Corpus, the largest open dataset for language model pre-training” and “the amount of collected data (2 trillion tokens) is suitable for pre-training of models of limited size” and “it is not directly suitable for task-specific fine-tuning”

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: “Common Corpus, which has been an ongoing effort since 2024” and “Continuing the work, we are currently collecting more data in European languages as part of the LLMs4EU project” and “We are developing in this direction, planning for enlargement of the corpora in African languages”
